claims.statement: The test suite is a single Vitest run: `pnpm test` maps to `vitest run` (no watch, no vitest config file), on Node >= 20 with ESM; tests import raw `src/*.ts` modules through the same NodeNext resolution the dev checkout uses, and the CLI has no runtime dependencies.

`pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` over both `src/**/*.ts` and `test/**/*.ts` under strict settings (`strict`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`), so tests are typechecked as strictly as production code and fixtures must omit optional properties (spread-with-... style) rather than assign undefined.

runMode tests inject a fake ModeCaller (vi.fn returning synthesized PipelineResult objects via the fakeResult helper and addUsageCall with a fixed $0.001/call cost), then assert dispatch counts, per-call role/model/messages/json/web fields, and result fields off caller.mock.calls — which is what makes budget-sequencing and two-pass dispatch assertions deterministic.

OpenRouter and bookmarks tests inject a fetchImpl (a parameter defaulting to global fetch on callOpenRouter and searchBookmarks) that returns canned Response objects; openrouter.test.ts asserts on request body tools/response_format and uses vi.useFakeTimers to advance the setTimeout-based retry backoff deterministically.

fetchXSignal accepts a spawnImpl + env dependency parameter so the Grok-agent child-process boundary is testable without a real `grok` binary; test/x-signal.test.ts pins the prompt contract and parsing fallbacks, and the only test file that uses a real subprocess is cli.test.ts via spawnSync.

cli.test.ts is the suite's single end-to-end test: it spawns `pnpm tsx src/cli.ts --json` with no prompt and pins the agent-facing error contract — exit status 1 with `{"error":{"message":"Missing prompt"}}` on stderr only.

test/args.test.ts pins parseArgs shapes and validation: defaults (mode auto, profile quality, outputStyle brief, empty web/x/bookmarks shapes), positional subcommand modes, flag families, `--` terminator, `wantsJson` pre-scan, and exact validation errors for missing prompt, unknown flags, invalid --max-cost, --output, --web-provider, and --x-network values.

test/config.test.ts pins defaults (quality-first Grok/Sonar aliases, web search enabled by default), config-file merge over defaults with env OPENROUTER_API_KEY override, resolveModel alias resolution, web option resolution precedence (--no-web > config; retrieve forces search on but not fetch; --web-fetch re-enables fetch), validation conflicts (allow+block lists, --web-fetch without search), assertWebToolsCompatible rejecting Perplexity expert overrides with web, and resolveCliOptions explicit-vs-config-default precedence.

test/modes.test.ts pins per-branch dispatch counts and model routing: single-call expert/fast/auto Grok, deepresearch to Sonar (with research→deepresearch deprecation warning and economy alias), multi's 5 calls with no web tools on any leg, and the --json+web two-pass (exactly 2 calls: research with tools then tool-less json_format, merged sources/warnings/usage) versus single-pass --json when web is off.

Under --max-cost, withBudget enforces the budget with a pre-check and a post-check around each call, throwing MaxCostExceededError immediately; tests pin that a single call aborts after one dispatch, and that multi's analysis legs switch from parallel to sequential (runSequential) so exactly the roles up to the crossing are dispatched — never more, so no further billable calls fire after the cap.

parseDecisionAnswer never throws for --json output: non-JSON content, non-object JSON such as a bare "-1.5E-05", and empty decision objects all degrade to warnings with answer omitted; tests pin these tolerances and the confidence coercion to medium unless exactly low/high.

Schema dispatch takes over the single-call path regardless of mode: tests pin that --schema overrides deepresearch and multi with warnings, uses exactly one schema call (not the 5-call multi fan-out), leaves schemaResult undefined (with a warning) when the model returns invalid JSON, and never parses a DecisionAnswer when --schema is set.

test/modes.test.ts pins the retrieve path activation: positional retrieve mode, --retrieve, and --output results|both on web-capable modes route to a retrieve call with json:true and web search enabled (fetch not forced); --output both adds a tool-less synthesis call; --retrieve/--output on deepresearch/multi is ignored with a warning; retrieve mode never parses DecisionAnswer.

test/openrouter.test.ts pins buildTools mapping: Grok models with search enabled get openrouter:web_search (with max_results/max_total_results and blockedDomains mapped to excluded_domains), optional openrouter:web_fetch keeps blocked_domains, Perplexity models and disabled search get no tools at all; and that response_format json_object is attached only when json && model supports it && no tools are present (never combined with server tools).

test/openrouter.test.ts pins the retry contract: up to 3 attempts for 429/>=500 responses and fetch TypeErrors, exponential backoff 2^attempt*1000ms with a Retry-After header (seconds) winning when larger, invalid response JSON surfaces a friendly OpenRouterError without retrying, and the request fails after 3 attempts with the provider error.

test/openrouter.test.ts pins status-to-error mapping: missing API key, 401/403 auth, 402 credits/quota, tool-use 404 (model does not support OpenRouter server tools), model-unavailable 404 with the selected model name and remediation hint, generic provider errors, and the merge of citations + url_citation annotations into deduped sources with normalized server_tool_use counters.

test/retrieval.test.ts pins parse tolerance and scoring: parseRetrieveContent returns empty results (never throws) for invalid JSON or non-array results, skips entries missing a url, preserves score/raw_content; resultsFromSources assigns descending citation-order scores in (0,1]; mergeRetrieveResults keeps model-emitted snippets, adds citation-only sources with empty content, and scores every unscored result.

test/x-signal.test.ts pins the X-signal contract: buildWhathappenedPrompt starts with the /whathappened topic line, requires the ## X_SIGNAL_MARKDOWN/## END_X_SIGNAL block, and encodes network off/prefer/strict; parseXSignalText extracts the marker block and reportPath from the labeled line or falls back to the full text with usedFallback:true; extractReportPath finds free-standing whathappened-reports HTML paths.

test/bookmarks.test.ts pins the TweetSmash client contract: env key candidate priority (TWEETSMASH_API_KEY then TWEETSMASH_TOKEN etc.), mapPost field mapping and author/tags extraction, relatedTerms derivation (authors/tags/query words, @ stripped, deduped), searchBookmarks skip semantics without a key, keyword q + vector_search_term query params, related-pass routing via author= versus q=, and formatBookmarksMarkdown section rendering.

For validating changes narrowly, the suite establishes the convention: match the existing injection seam (ModeCaller fake for runMode dispatch, fetchImpl for OpenRouter/bookmark request logic, spawnImpl for X, pure-function tests for retrieval/scoring), assert on what was dispatched (caller.mock.calls) and exact result fields, keep full toThrow/toContain failure messages where the string is the contract, respect exactOptionalPropertyTypes in fixtures, and keep cli.test.ts the only real-subprocess test.
